002c9507fffe090b.question: Which privacy law applies to what booking keeps, in New York, and what does it require of booking and of the privacy notice (R6, R10)? Background read on 2026-10-20, for the adviser to confirm, not settled: HIPAA binds a provider that sends claims or other standard transactions electronically, so a clinic paid only by its patients may fall outside it unless it does so for anything, e-prescribing or a laboratory included; New York's SHIELD Act asks for reasonable security of the private information it keeps and notice of a breach, and was read as covering medical information since 2025; a New York health information privacy act was vetoed in December 2025 and a revised bill was pending in 2026; tracking scripts on a booking page are where federal guidance has been strictest.
002c9507fffe090b.why: booking takes a person's details for a medical appointment, and the law decides how they are kept, which tools the website may use on the booking pages, and what the notice must say

0159edefb9b0eff2.name: Button
0159edefb9b0eff2.purpose: What a person presses to do something: book, save, sign in, cancel. One primary button per screen or part, for the step that moves the work on; secondary for the other choices; small inside a row of a table or a list.
0159edefb9b0eff2.rules: - At least 44 pixels high, 32 when small, and never narrower than its words. - It says the verb, in sentence case: Book, Save, Cancel -- never OK. - A link that only leads somewhere stays a link; a button does something. - Its look is the proposal of the foundations, 2026-10-20, to be changed with them. (foundations)

0944af9ff52e5182.question: Which rules on health advertising apply to what the website says about the services and about longevity (R2, R4)? Background read on 2026-10-20, for the adviser to confirm, not settled: New York's Education Law 6530(27) and the Regents' rule 8 NYCRR 29.1 forbid a physician's advertising that is false or misleading, guarantees a result, or claims what cannot be substantiated, allow a patient's testimonial only with their written consent and the rule's conditions, and ask that a copy of each advertisement be kept for a year after it last appears; the FTC asks that a health claim rest on competent and reliable scientific evidence.
0944af9ff52e5182.why: a claim the rules do not allow puts the clinic at risk, the longevity wording is where one is likeliest, and the staff change the words themselves (R13), so the rules may also decide who approves a change and what is kept of it

a2606f1d0f0d0fd3.question: Which rules on prices apply to patients who pay themselves, and what must the website show to meet them (R6, R7)? Background read on 2026-10-20, for the adviser to confirm, not settled: under the federal No Surprises Act a provider tells a patient who pays themselves that a good faith estimate of the cost is available -- in a notice on its website, in the office and when a visit is scheduled -- and gives one when a visit is booked some days ahead or when asked; CMS publishes a model notice.
a2606f1d0f0d0fd3.why: R7 shows a price per appointment type, and these rules may ask for a notice on the website and an estimate with each booking, which would change booking (R6) and the confirmation

bcd422bb87e31977.rules: - The time in the clinic's own time, written 10:00 AM. (R14) - The slots of a day sit in a row and wrap, earliest first; a screen reader hears each as a toggle button, pressed or not. - Its look is the proposal of the foundations, 2026-10-20, to be changed with them. (foundations)

db41b0f22ad94523.name: Book an appointment
db41b0f22ad94523.purpose: A visitor books an appointment type with a doctor at a free time, signing in or creating an account on the way, and has it confirmed on the next screen.
db41b0f22ad94523.steps: 1. The visitor chooses an appointment type and sees its price; booking asks for no medical details, and says it is not for emergencies. SC8, R6, R7, R11 2. They choose a doctor who gives the type, or any, and a day; booking shows the free times, or, with none that day, the nearest days that have one. SC8, R14, R6 3. They choose a time and Continue; Continue with no time asks for one. SC8, R6 4. Signed out, they sign in, and the time is kept. SC9, R16, R6 5. New to NovaLife, they create an account with their name, date of birth, email, phone and a password, and the time is kept. SC21, R16, R6 6. They check the type, the doctor, the time and the price, which they pay themselves at the visit, and book. SC10, R6, R7 7. If the time was just booked by someone else, nothing is booked, and the nearest free times show. SC10, R6 8. If the booking fails, nothing is booked, what was chosen is kept, and they try again. SC10, R6 9. The next screen confirms it: the type, the doctor, the day and the time. SC11, R6
